fall-2026/human-development/brains-maps-.title: Chapter One Brain Map
fall-2026/human-development/brains-maps-.description:
Pg. 9-12Three Specific ContextsChapter 1 - Theories of Development & Genetics
#HumanDevlopment #BrainMap Theories of DevelopmentMultidirectional - We don't just grow in one area, and we don't just stay at a standstill either. Humans can grow in multiple areas, in one area, or actually decay or have loss as well.Lifelong - You don't reach 28 years old and stay stuck like that forever. You grow in some ways, lose other things (coughmalepatterbaldnesscoughcough), and that means you can become a totally different individual at 86 or something.Multidimensional: We can change across three different domains or dimensions (not literal); physical, cognitive, and psychosocial.Characterized by Plasticity - How we can accept change basicallyMultidisciplinary - Double Dipping in the party dip but in a Human Development lens. He basically recognizes that people can take multiple perspectives into account.Normative history-graded influences: The period of time in which you were born can have a great deal of importance to your individual characteristics (ex. Baby Boomers -> Talk on Phone, Gen Z -> Life is Phone)Normative age-graded influences: An age grade means stages like toddler or teenagerNon-normative life influences:MulticontextualPsychosocial - How we interact with those around us.Cognitive - Changes in our minds, like learning a new language, or taking a Human Development class :)All three of these Domains interact with each other and change one another. Failure in one can cause others to faulter, and the inverse is also applicable.Physical - Biological development (puberty, major illness).
Socioeconomic status is also another context, but Paul Baltes didn't feel like adding it in his list I guess. Socioeconomic just means your place in society and tax brackets (businessman vs ceo) also has an effect on your development.

info_maxNodeRadius.description: How large should the largest nodes be? Nodes are sized by how many links they have. The larger a node is the more it will attract other nodes. This can be used to create a good grouping around the most important nodes.
